name: Loarki
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog: retired/spurious entry duplicating Gade Lohar [gda]; no descriptive refs listed.

sources.note: Nothing; tertiary, cites Ethnologue and Glottolog only.

sources.citation: Zubair, M. 2016. [Wadiyari phonology MA thesis] (on file: ling/synchro/tropics/), sections 2.3.2 and 2.5 on Jeffery (ed.) 1999 Sindh Survey Month.
sources.note: Nothing on Loarki stress; documents that 'Loar' data come from the unpublished 1996-99 SIL Sindh survey (125-item wordlists, sociolinguistic questionnaires) and that Jeffery 1999 set up 'Loarki' as its own Rajasthani subgroup.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, ch. 10 (on file:).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no Harvard e-access found (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Loarki and Gade Lohar appear only in the Ethnologue-derived classification list (p. 552); no accent data given for either.

sources.citation: Sharma, J.C. 1971. Pronouns in Gade Lohar dialect. In H.S. Biligiri (ed.), Papers and talks presented and delivered at the Summer School of Linguistics 1970, 73-76. Mysore: Central Institute of Indian Languages.
sources.note: Nothing; introduction on the community (Gade Lohars nomadising around Delhi) and pronoun paradigms only; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages loar1234 (Loarki, Bookkeeping) and gade1236 (Gade Lohar).
sources.note: Nothing; states Loarki [lrk] duplicates Gade Lohar [gda], citing Sharma 1988; Gade Lohar refs = Sharma 1988 only.

sources.citation: Sharma, Jagdish Chander. 1973. Nominal and verbal inflection in the dialect of the Gade Lohars. Indian Linguistics 34.

sources.citation: Jeffery, David (ed.). 1999. Sindh Survey Month. Karachi: SIL ms. (survey of 34 groups in Sindh incl. 'Loar'; wordlists and sociolinguistic questionnaires).

sources.note: The only primary data on Loarki as spoken in Sindh (basis of the Ethnologue lrk entry); phonetic wordlists might show stress marking, though no prose phonology is expected.
